title: Image Carousel Component
prompt: Design a reusable image carousel for product pages: one big photo at a time, arrows, dots and swipe, used by several teams in the same codebase.

clarify.q: How many images per carousel: 5, 20 or 500?
clarify.why: Up to ~30 we can render every slide shell and lazy-load images. Hundreds (a photo album) need virtualised slides and paged loading from the server.

clarify.q: Only images, or any content (video, cards, text)?
clarify.why: Images-only lets us own srcset and sizing. Arbitrary children push us to a render-prop or slot API and stop us assuming heights.

clarify.q: Does a parent need to drive it, for example a thumbnail strip or a colour picker that jumps to slide 4?
clarify.why: That is the controlled-component case: the parent owns the index. Most teams won't need it, so the component must also work uncontrolled.
Autoplay brings WCAG rules: a visible pause button, pause on hover and focus, and none at all under prefers-reduced-motion. Without it, the design is simpler.

clarify.q: One slide per view, or several (peek of the next slide, 3 per row on desktop)?
clarify.why: Slides per view changes the maths of positions, which slides count as 'visible', and what 'next' means.

clarify.q: Infinite loop, or stop at the ends?
clarify.why: A loop needs cloned slides or index wrapping, which complicates focus order and screen reader position ('20 of 20' then '1 of 20').

clarify.q: Do we need a full-screen lightbox with zoom?
clarify.why: Zoom adds pinch gestures that fight with swipe. It usually belongs in a separate component that shares the same state hook.

functional: Show one image at a time with Previous and Next buttons and a position indicator ('3 of 12' and dots).
Swipe left or right on touch screens; drag with a mouse is optional.
Arrow keys move between slides when the carousel has focus.
Work both uncontrolled (manages its own index) and controlled (parent passes index and handles changes).
Optional autoplay with a visible pause/play button.
Images load at the right resolution for the screen and device pixel ratio.
nonFunctional: First slide is often the page's LCP element: it must not be lazy-loaded and should paint within 2.5 s on slow 4G.
Zero layout shift: the carousel reserves its height before any image loads (CLS 0).
Swipe tracks the finger at 60 fps (120 Hz where supported) using only compositor-friendly transforms.
WCAG 2.2 AA: keyboard operable, announced position, pausable motion, respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Under 5 KB gzipped of JavaScript; works (shows the first image) before JavaScript loads.
Supports right-to-left layouts: 'next' moves the other way.
outOfScope: Pinch-to-zoom lightbox (a sibling component using the same state hook).
Image upload, cropping and the image processing pipeline.
Video slides with their own playback controls.

assumptions: Product gallery of 20 photos, 4:5 aspect ratio
Mobile slot 390 CSS px wide at DPR 3; desktop slot 600 CSS px at DPR 2
A 1200 px wide WebP or AVIF photo is ~120 KB
Slow 4G: 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps ≈ 200 KB/s; server-rendered HTML arrives at ~800 ms

steps.label: Load every image eagerly
steps.result: ≈ 12 s of bandwidth, competing with the LCP image: never do this

steps.label: Load current slide plus neighbours
steps.math: 3 × 120 KB = 360 KB ÷ 200 KB/s ≈ 1.8 s; first slide alone 120 KB ≈ 0.6 s
steps.result: First image in ~0.6 s; neighbours ready before most users swipe

steps.label: Which width to request
steps.result: 1200w variant for both; offer 400w, 800w, 1200w, 1600w in srcset and let sizes pick

steps.label: LCP of the first slide
steps.math: 800 ms HTML + 150 ms RTT + 600 ms transfer
steps.result: ≈ 1.55 s if the img is in the server HTML and eager. Lazy or JS-inserted adds hydration time and can miss 2.5 s

steps.label: Decoded image memory
steps.math: 1200 × 1500 px × 4 bytes = 7.2 MB each. Window of current ± 2 = 5 images ≈ 36 MB; all 20 ≈ 144 MB
steps.result: Keep a small window decoded on low-memory phones

steps.label: Frame budget while dragging
steps.math: 60 Hz → 16.7 ms per frame; 120 Hz → 8.3 ms
steps.result: Only change transform during a drag; any layout per frame risks dropped frames on 120 Hz screens

steps.label: Swipe thresholds
steps.math: Distance: 25% of 390 px ≈ 98 px. Velocity: a 60 px flick in 200 ms = 0.3 px/ms
steps.result: Commit to the next slide if dragged > 25% of width or released faster than 0.3 px/ms

estimates.takeaway: Bytes decide everything. Loading all 20 photos costs ~12 s on slow 4G. Loading the current photo and its neighbours costs ~1.8 s, and the first photo alone ~0.6 s. So: eager, high-priority first slide in the server HTML, neighbours preloaded, the rest only when approached. Reserve the box with aspect-ratio for zero CLS. During a drag, touch only transform.

api.body: { items: { id, alt, width, height, srcSet, sizes? }[], label: string, slidesPerView = 1, loop = false, preload = 1 (neighbours each side) }
api.note: width and height are required so the box can reserve space. label is required; a carousel without a name is an accessibility bug.

api.body: Controlled: { index, onIndexChange }. Uncontrolled: { defaultIndex = 0 }. Optional: { autoplay?: { intervalMs = 6000 } }
api.note: A useControllableState hook picks the mode once at mount; dev warning if it switches.

api.returns: void; in controlled mode, nothing moves until the parent updates index
api.note: The reason lets analytics tell swipes from autoplay, and lets the parent ignore autoplay changes if it wants.
For rare cases like 'jump to the photo of the selected colour' in uncontrolled mode.

api.body: renderSlide(item, { index, isActive, isNear }) ; renderControls({ index, count, goTo, isPlaying, toggle })
api.note: Escape hatches for teams with non-image slides or custom dots, while state, gestures and ARIA stay inside.

api.body: Image URLs use an image CDN: /img/{mediaId}?w=1200&fmt=auto
api.returns: 200 { items: [{ id, alt, width, height, dominantColor }] }
api.note: Small lists need no pagination. Albums with hundreds of photos use ?cursor=…&limit=30 and fetch the next page when within 5 slides of the end.

entities.name: CarouselState
entities.store: Component state via a useCarousel hook
entities.why: One hook used by the carousel, a thumbnail strip and a lightbox, so they share behaviour and stay in sync.

entities.name: MediaItem
entities.why: Intrinsic size gives aspect-ratio before load. Alt text is content, so it comes from the server, not the component.

entities.name: URL state (optional)
entities.why: Lets people share 'the third photo'. Use replaceState so swiping doesn't fill the back history.

data.note: pausedBy as a set avoids a common bug: hover ends and autoplay resumes even though the user pressed Pause. Autoplay runs only when the set is empty. loaded only grows: once an image was allowed to load, we keep its src so swiping back doesn't refetch. On low-memory devices (navigator.deviceMemory ≤ 2) we instead release images more than 2 slides away.

hld.summary:
The carousel is a headless useCarousel hook plus a thin styled component. The hook owns the index (controlled or not), autoplay timers, pointer gesture maths and keyboard handling. It returns props to spread on the parts. The component renders a viewport with overflow hidden, a track moved with transform: translateX, one slide per item, and the controls.

Every slide box exists from the start with aspect-ratio from the item's width and height, so layout never moves. Only slides inside the preload window get a real src. Slide 0 is server-rendered as a plain eager img with fetchpriority=high, so it paints before JavaScript arrives. A visually hidden live region announces 'Slide 3 of 12' after user-driven changes.

diagram.title: Component tree
diagram.src:
flowchart TD
  ROOT["Carousel (section, carousel role description)"] --> HOOK["useCarousel (index, gestures, autoplay)"]
  ROOT --> VP["Viewport (overflow hidden)"]
  VP --> TRACK["Track (transform translateX)"]
  TRACK --> SLIDE["Slide (group, 3 of 12)"]
  SLIDE --> IMG["ResponsiveImage (srcset, aspect-ratio)"]
  ROOT --> PREV[Previous button]
  ROOT --> NEXT[Next button]
  ROOT --> DOTS[Dot buttons]
  ROOT --> PLAY[Pause and play button]
  ROOT --> LIVE[Live region]
  HOOK -.->|props| TRACK
  HOOK -.->|onIndexChange| PARENT[Parent or thumbnail strip]

flows.title: Swiping to the next photo
steps: pointerdown on the track: record x and time, call setPointerCapture.
pointermove: once horizontal movement passes 10 px and exceeds vertical, lock to horizontal; track follows the finger with translateX in a requestAnimationFrame.
pointerup: if dx > 25% of width or speed > 0.3 px/ms, go next; otherwise spring back.
Index changes (or onIndexChange is called in controlled mode); slide i+2 enters the preload window and its src is set.
Track animates with a 250 ms CSS transition (0 ms under reduced motion); the live region says 'Photo 4 of 12'.

flows.title: Controlled by a thumbnail strip
steps: Parent holds index in its state and passes it to both the carousel and the strip.
User taps thumbnail 7: the strip calls the parent setter; the carousel receives index 7.
Carousel animates to 7 and adds 6 and 8 to the preload window.
User swipes the carousel: onIndexChange(8, { reason: 'swipe' }) fires; the parent updates; the strip scrolls 8 into view.

flows.title: Keyboard and screen reader use
steps: Tab reaches the Previous button, then Next, dots and Pause, in visual order.
Left and Right arrows change slides when focus is inside the carousel; Home and End jump to the ends.
Offscreen slides are inert, so Tab never lands on a link inside a hidden slide.
If focus was on a control in the old slide, it moves to the new slide's group (tabindex -1) so it isn't lost.

deepDives.title: API that is both controlled and uncontrolled
deepDives.problem: Most teams want <Carousel items={photos} /> and nothing more. A few need the parent to own the index to sync thumbnails, a colour picker or the URL. Two components drift apart; one component with two half-working modes causes bugs where the prop and internal state disagree.

options.name: Uncontrolled only, plus a ref
options.how: Internal index; parents call ref.goTo(i) and listen to onIndexChange.
pros: Simplest API
No mode confusion
cons: Two sources of truth when a parent also tracks the index
Can't render from URL state on the server cleanly

options.name: Controlled only
pros: One source of truth; easy to test
cons: Every caller writes the same useState boilerplate
Easy to forget the handler and get a frozen carousel

options.name: Both, via a controllable-state hook
options.how: If index is defined, use it and only call onIndexChange; otherwise keep internal state seeded by defaultIndex. Same pattern as native input value/defaultValue.
pros: Easy default, full control when needed
Familiar to React developers
cons: Must detect and warn about switching modes
Two code paths to test

options.name: Headless hook plus thin component
options.how: Export useCarousel for teams who want custom markup, and Carousel built on it.
pros: Custom designs without forking
Behaviour and ARIA live in one place
cons: Larger public surface to version and document

deepDives.choice: Both modes through a controllable-state hook, with the headless hook exported too. Rules: the mode is fixed at mount; onIndexChange always fires with a reason; in controlled mode nothing moves until the parent updates index; out-of-range indexes are clamped (or wrapped when loop). If only one product team used it, I'd ship uncontrolled plus a ref and add control later.

deepDives.title: Lazy loading neighbours and responsive images
deepDives.problem: The first photo is the LCP element and must load early. The rest should not compete with it, yet a user who swipes should never see an empty slide. Native lazy loading decides by distance from the viewport, and slides hidden inside a horizontal overflow container are handled differently across browsers.

options.name: Native loading=lazy on all but the first
options.how: Slide 0 eager with fetchpriority=high; all others loading=lazy with srcset and sizes.
pros: No JavaScript
Fine when slides sit in a scroll-snap container
cons: Look-ahead distance isn't ours to tune
Inconsistent for slides moved with transforms

options.name: Index window
options.how: Set src only for slides within index ± preload; grow the window as the user moves.
pros: Predictable: the next slide is always ready
Works the same for transform and scroll layouts
cons: Needs JavaScript; before hydration only the first slide shows

options.name: Preload on intent
options.how: On pointerdown or hover over Next, start loading the next slide's image (new Image() with the same srcset).
pros: Cheap; loads only when the user is about to move
cons: Too late on slow 4G: 0.6 s per photo
Hover doesn't exist on touch

deepDives.choice: Index window with preload = 1, raised to 2 on fast connections (navigator.connection.effectiveType 4g and no Save-Data), plus intent preloading as a cheap extra. Every image uses srcset with 400w to 1600w and sizes='(min-width: 768px) 600px, 100vw', so a phone at DPR 3 takes 1200w, not 1600w. Boxes use aspect-ratio and a dominant-colour background, so an unloaded slide looks intentional, not broken. If the carousel were below the fold, the first slide would be lazy too.

deepDives.title: Touch gestures: scroll-snap or JavaScript track
deepDives.problem: The swipe must follow the finger 1:1, must not block vertical page scrolling, and must decide between 'next' and 'snap back' in a way that feels natural. Doing it wrong either janks or traps the page scroll.

options.name: CSS scroll-snap
options.how: Track is overflow-x: auto with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; each slide scroll-snap-align: center. JavaScript only reads which slide is in view (scrollend or IntersectionObserver) and calls scrollTo for buttons.
pros: Native momentum and feel on every platform
Scroll runs off the main thread
Works before JavaScript loads
cons: Hard to do infinite loop
Fine control of thresholds and easing is limited
Programmatic scroll events need care to avoid feedback loops in controlled mode

options.name: Pointer events and transform
options.how: touch-action: pan-y on the track; pointer events compute dx; translateX follows in requestAnimationFrame; release decides by distance and velocity.
pros: Full control: loop, thresholds, rubber-banding at ends
Same code for mouse and touch
cons: You own the physics; easy to make it feel wrong
Main-thread work during the drag

deepDives.choice: Scroll-snap by default: it gives native feel, works before hydration and is cheapest to maintain. Switch to the pointer and transform track when loop is on or the design needs custom physics. In that mode: touch-action: pan-y so vertical scrolling still belongs to the browser; lock the axis after 10 px; use setPointerCapture; commit at 25% of width or 0.3 px/ms; invert dx in RTL. In both modes, a drag shorter than 5 px is treated as a click so links in slides still work.

deepDives.title: Accessibility: semantics, focus, announcements and motion
deepDives.problem: Carousels are a famous accessibility failure. Typical bugs: unlabelled arrow icons, Tab landing inside invisible slides, nothing announced on change, and autoplay that moves content while a screen-reader user is still reading it.

options.name: Grouped slides pattern
options.how: Container: section with aria-roledescription='carousel' and aria-label. Each slide: role=group, aria-roledescription='slide', aria-label='3 of 12'. Buttons with real text labels. Offscreen slides get the inert attribute.
pros: Clear structure: users know where they are
inert removes hidden slides from Tab order and the accessibility tree
cons: Live announcements must be handled separately

options.name: Tabs pattern for dots
options.how: Dots are a role=tablist; each dot a tab controlling a slide tabpanel; arrow keys move between tabs.
pros: Rich keyboard model on the dots
Good when slides are distinct sections
cons: Heavier semantics than a photo gallery needs
Screen reader users hear 'tab 3 of 12' for photos

deepDives.choice: Grouped slides pattern, with dots as plain buttons labelled 'Show photo 3' and aria-current on the active one. Announce with a polite live region: on during manual navigation, off while autoplay runs (otherwise it talks every 6 s). Autoplay: visible Pause button first in tab order; pause on hover, on focus inside, when the tab is hidden, and permanently once the user presses Pause; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, where slide changes also happen without animation. This meets WCAG 2.2.2 (pause, stop, hide). Buttons and dots have 44 × 44 px touch targets, even if the visible dot is 8 px.

failures: First slide is lazy-loaded and LCP jumps to 3+ s
Slide 0 eager in the server HTML with fetchpriority=high; lint rule or test that checks it.
Keep the reserved box with its dominant colour and alt text visible; offer a retry on tap; never collapse the slide.
Carousel shifts the page when images load
Width and height from the API set aspect-ratio; the viewport height never depends on the image.
Controlled parent forgets onIndexChange, carousel looks frozen
Dev-mode warning when index is passed without a handler, like React does for inputs.
Vertical page scroll gets captured by the carousel
touch-action: pan-y and axis locking; never preventDefault on touchmove before the axis is known.
Missing or empty alt text from the CMS
Required in the API type; fallback to the product name plus 'photo 3 of 12'; report missing alts in CMS tooling.
scale: Hundreds of photos (albums): virtualise slides (render only index ± 3 boxes), page the media API with a cursor, keep a capped set of decoded images.
Many teams using it: move it into the design system as a headless hook plus styled component, with visual and accessibility tests in CI.
Heavy pages with several carousels: only the one in view preloads neighbours; others stay at the first slide until they enter the viewport.

answer: Unit test the hook: index clamping, controlled vs uncontrolled, pausedBy logic with fake timers.
Component tests with Testing Library: arrow keys, Home and End, aria-label '3 of 12', inert on hidden slides.
Automated axe checks plus a manual pass with VoiceOver and NVDA; visual regression for RTL.
Next moves visually left; arrows swap meaning; use logical CSS properties.
In the transform track, invert dx; scroll-snap handles RTL natively.
Icons for Previous and Next are mirrored; the position text stays '3 of 12'.
Index wraps with modulo; the transform track clones one slide at each end and jumps without animation after the transition.
Clones are aria-hidden and inert so screen readers don't count them.
Announce position from the real index, not the clone's.

followups.q: What would you put in the server-rendered HTML?
answer: The full first slide img and the slide boxes with aspect-ratio, so it looks right before JavaScript.
Buttons rendered but harmless until hydrated, or rendered disabled.
With scroll-snap, the whole carousel works without JavaScript.

followups.q: Why not use an existing carousel library?
answer: Often the right call: check bundle size, accessibility (labels, inert, live region), RTL and controlled support.
Many libraries ship 20–40 KB and hard-code markup that fights the design system.
If you adopt one, wrap it so swapping later doesn't touch every caller.

mistakes: Lazy-loading the first slide, which is usually the LCP image.
Images without width and height, so the carousel jumps as each loads.
Animating left or margin instead of transform during drags.
Autoplay with no pause button and no reduced-motion handling.
Leaving hidden slides focusable, so Tab disappears into invisible links.

mid: Wrote the props: items with alt, width, height; index/defaultIndex; onIndexChange
Loaded the first image eagerly and the others lazily, with srcset
Reserved space with aspect-ratio to avoid CLS
Labelled the buttons, added keyboard arrows, and announced the position
Handled swipe with a distance threshold
senior: Explained controlled vs uncontrolled with the value/defaultValue pattern and dev warnings
Compared scroll-snap with a pointer-event transform track and chose with reasons
Used touch-action: pan-y, axis locking and a velocity threshold
Made offscreen slides inert and kept focus from being lost on slide change
Covered autoplay: pause button, pause on hover and focus, reduced motion, live region off while autoplaying
staff: Split it into a headless hook and a styled component for the design system
Did the byte and memory arithmetic and tuned the preload window to connection and device memory
Covered RTL, loop clones and their accessibility, and a testing strategy
